headline: Medical costs pressure margins, but guidance raised
summary_short: Elevance Health's Q2 FY2026 total revenue was $50.47B (+1.4% y/y) but operating gain fell to $1.76B (-27.3% y/y) as the benefit expense ratio rose 80bp to 89.7%, pulling diluted EPS to $6.71 (-13.1% y/y). The company nonetheless raised full-year 2026 adjusted diluted EPS guidance to at least $27.00.
summary_long: Operating revenue grew on higher Health Benefits premium yields and CarelonRx growth, offset by anticipated Medicare Advantage, Medicaid and Employer Group risk membership declines. Operating gain fell 27.3% y/y as the benefit expense ratio rose 80bp on elevated government-business medical cost trend, partly offset by better Individual ACA performance; adjusted operating expense ratio rose 100bp on workforce investment. Diluted EPS of $6.71 (adjusted $7.45) declined y/y despite results beating the company's own outlook. Cash grew to $10.23B; the company repurchased $234M of stock and paid a $1.72/share dividend. Management raised FY2026 diluted EPS guidance to at least $20.10, adjusted diluted EPS to at least $27.00, and operating cash flow guidance to at least $6.0B.

drivers.explanation: Higher premium yields in Health Benefits and growth in CarelonRx product revenue, partially offset by anticipated declines in Medicare Advantage, Medicaid, and Employer Group risk membership.

Benefit expense ratio rose 80bp y/y on elevated medical cost trend in government businesses, partially offset by improved Individual ACA performance; adjusted operating expense ratio rose 100bp on workforce investment.

GAAP diluted EPS fell y/y despite results exceeding the company's own outlook and a roughly $0.80/share net below-the-line benefit, reflecting the lower operating gain flowing through to the bottom line.
Operating cash flow reflected timing of a state Medicaid pass-through payment plus underlying business strength.

Results beat the company's own outlook and management raised FY2026 diluted EPS, adjusted diluted EPS, and operating cash flow guidance, while accelerating investment in medical-cost management, member experience, and Carelon's value-based solutions.
